name: Native copper working at Çayönü Tepesi
summary: Pre-Pottery Neolithic residents of Çayönü worked native copper into ornaments and small tools. The excavations also record a separate malachite craft.
description: At Çayönü Tepesi in southeastern Anatolia, people worked native copper into ornaments and small tools during the Pre-Pottery Neolithic. The excavators distinguish worked metal from malachite ornaments and locate the first clear worked finds in Grill Buildings and basal-pit contexts. Later workshop areas in the Channelled and Cobble-Paved subphases contained objects at several stages of production.

impact.note: Native copper ornaments and small tools were made in a few Neolithic villages of Anatolia and the northern Levant (reach 1); they added a material for beads, awls and hooks without changing how people lived (depth 1); smelting arose later in the same region, but the cited study reports that copper use did not develop continuously, so only limited succession is counted (generativity 1).

date.label: 8200-7500 BC
date.basis: The 8200–7500 BCE interval is from Muşkara and Aydın's comparative table. The excavation report assigns individual objects to relative building subphases.

events.statement: Çayönü's Pre-Pottery Neolithic levels yielded worked native copper ornaments and small tools. The excavators place the first clear worked finds in the Grill Buildings and basal-pit contexts, and discuss metallographic indications of annealing in native copper.

evidence.supports: Çayönü 8200-7500 BC (Yalçın 2000) Anatolia, SE Native copper Malachite Annealing, coldworking

evidence.locator: pp. 15–19, distribution by building subphase and Figs. 1 and 4
evidence.supports: Early worked copper finds and later workshop areas are documented stratigraphically. The report identifies worked native copper separately from malachite and refers to metallographic indications of annealing.

events.caveats: The comparative dates serve as approximate context. A calibrated date for the first worked object and a secure geological source remain open.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The excavation report places first clear worked finds in Grill Buildings and basal pits and cites indications of annealing. Read the original metallographic sample list and identify individual annealed objects against the excavators' subphase inventory.

evidence.supports: The excavators report early worked finds and cite Stech and Maddin et al. for metallurgy.

unresolved.note: Whether the table's 8200-7500 BC is calibrated, and which building phases the worked copper comes from.

Whether later Anatolian smelting (the study gives Yumuktepe, early fifth millennium BC) grew out of this native copper working or followed a break; the study quotes Yener that copper use did not develop steadily.
Aşıklı Höyük, named in the lead, appears in the same table with native copper beads, but its dates are scrambled in the extracted text and were not used.

research.note: Muşkara and Aydın write that Neolithic settlements in Anatolia present the earliest metallurgical activities and name Çayönü as the site that yielded the earliest metal objects; Gre Fılla, 90 km away, has overlapping dates (8349-7502 cal BC) but its copper treatment was not determined, and the primary Çayönü reports were not opened.
